Stated Claim / Post Context:
JetBlue pilot thought he smelled 'dirty socks' in his cabin...  but he claims it was really 'toxic air' that left him disabled, destroyed his career and may threaten millions of flyers

Capt Clayton Adamy claims he initially noticed a 'dirty sock' odor aboard the Embraer ERJ-190 he was ferrying from Vermont to New York in 2023, just days after Thanksgiving.

Actual Article Body:
By JUSTIN ROHRLICH

Published:  08:40 AEDT, 16 November 2026   |  Updated:  08:40 AEDT, 16 November 2026

A JetBlue pilot is no longer able to fly after being 'incurably, totally and permanently disabled' by toxic fumes inside his aircraft, according to a federal lawsuit obtained by the Daily Mail.

Capt Clayton Adamy claims he initially noticed a 'dirty sock' odor aboard the Embraer ERJ-190 he was ferrying from Vermont to New York in 2023, just days after Thanksgiving.

Adamy, 36, said he woke up the morning after the flight feeling like his lungs were 'filled with razor blades.'

In the months and years that followed, he claims he suffered spates of fainting spells and an irregular heartbeat, the Kentucky native's complaint stated.

Adamy said in the complaint that he was diagnosed with 'reactive airway dysfunction' due to the inhalation of noxious gases and that it 'precludes him from operating aircraft.'

Other symptoms he suffers include ongoing shortness of breath, a persistent cough, chest tightness and wheezing, according to the complaint.

The filing added that he is 'recognized as fully disabled by Workers' Compensation' and may never be able to take to the skies again.

If proven to be valid, Adamy's complaint may serve as a warning to the millions of frequent flyers who use JetBlue each year, drawing attention to concerns over the air they breathe at 30,000 feet.

JetBlue Capt. Clayton Adamy, 36, blames a 2023 'fume event' for ruining his health and career (source: LinkedIn)

Several videos are circulating on social media of people warning about toxic 'fume events' on flights (source: TikTok/ jerseygirlattorney)

Since the 1980s, there have been hundreds of documented incidents on various airlines in which hazardous fluids such as synthetic engine oil, hydraulic fluid or de-icing chemicals enter a plane's breathable air through leaky seals or gaskets, according to the peer-reviewed academic journal Toxics.

According to the complaint, Embraer planes, which are flown by most major airlines including American, Delta, United, British Airways, Japan Air Lines and KLM, feature air compressors that 'bleed' air into the cabin and flight deck without filtering it first, a design it says renders the air 'highly toxic and unfit for human consumption.'

Descriptions of the smell vary, with some comparing it to 'wet dog' or 'Cheetos.'
